candidates.sector_or_industry: AI accelerators / GPUs / accelerated computing platforms
candidates.theme_relation: Primary public-market supplier of AI accelerator platforms used in training and inference; upstream demand signal for HBM, advanced packaging, networking, power, and cooling.
Critical manufacturing bottleneck for leading-edge AI accelerators and advanced packaging capacity, including CoWoS, InFO, SoIC, and related packaging technologies.
Scarce lithography equipment supplier for advanced logic and DRAM nodes supporting the AI infrastructure buildout.
HBM and data-center DRAM supplier tied directly to AI accelerator memory bandwidth requirements.
Major AI compute demand owner through Azure, OpenAI-related infrastructure, Copilot, GitHub, Microsoft 365, and enterprise AI services.
AWS is a primary channel for enterprise AI compute demand, while Amazon's internal AI investments create additional captive infrastructure demand.

candidates.sector_or_industry: Cloud hyperscaler / internet platform / AI model operator
candidates.theme_relation: AI compute buyer and seller through Google Cloud, Gemini/DeepMind, internal search workloads, and TPU-based infrastructure.
AI chip architectures increase rack power density and cooling requirements, creating demand for mission-critical data-center power and thermal systems.
AI clusters require high-bandwidth low-latency networking; Arista maps to Ethernet AI networking and data-center switching infrastructure.

OCI growth, large remaining performance obligations, and AI customer commitments make Oracle a direct public proxy for AI compute capacity demand, with execution and financing risk requiring later validation.
Pure-play rented AI compute capacity provider; useful as a high-beta demand and utilization indicator for GPU clusters, power, and data-center buildout.

candidates.sector_or_industry: Electrical equipment / switchgear / power distribution systems
candidates.theme_relation: AI data-center campuses require medium-voltage switchgear and integrated electrical systems; this node can become constrained when power interconnection and electrical-equipment lead times stretch.

candidates.sector_or_industry: Electrical connection, enclosures, rack power, and liquid cooling infrastructure
candidates.theme_relation: AI accelerators raise rack power density and thermal loads, increasing demand for coolant distribution units, manifolds, PDUs, racks, and related infrastructure.
AI and high-performance computing increase heat loads, pushing demand toward high-density cooling systems including air, hybrid, and liquid cooling.

candidates.sector_or_industry: HVAC, thermal management, and data-center cooling
candidates.theme_relation: High-density AI workloads create demand for end-to-end cooling systems from chillers and controls to direct-to-chip and immersion cooling.

candidates.sector_or_industry: Backup power generation / mission-critical power equipment
candidates.theme_relation: AI compute clusters increase uptime and backup-power requirements, making emergency standby generation part of hyperscaler data-center capex.
If time-to-power becomes a binding AI data-center constraint, onsite fuel-cell power can capture demand from operators facing grid-interconnection delays.

candidates.sector_or_industry: Electronics manufacturing services / data-center hardware manufacturing
candidates.theme_relation: AI capex translates into compute and networking hardware programs where manufacturing execution and hyperscaler supply-chain capacity can become bottlenecks.

candidates.sector_or_industry: Mechanical and electrical contracting / building systems
candidates.theme_relation: AI data-center projects require scarce mechanical, electrical, HVAC, and construction execution capacity before compute clusters can become operational.

candidates.sector_or_industry: Enterprise AI software / data integration platforms
candidates.theme_relation: Enterprise AI monetization layer where constraints are data readiness, integration, governance, security, workflow deployment, and measurable ROI.
Hyperscaler AI buildouts require complex procurement of electrical distribution, fiber/connectivity, switchgear, cabling, automation, and utility-grid materials.

coverage_gaps: The provided Layer 1B candidate block appears truncated; this Layer 1C universe likely under-represents AI accelerator peers, semiconductor equipment, advanced packaging suppliers, substrates/interposers, optical components, test equipment, and Asian public-market listings.

Need a dedicated semiconductor component pass: HBM suppliers beyond Micron, HBM test/bonding equipment, advanced substrates, CCL, interposers, reticles, EDA, sockets, probe cards, and advanced packaging OSATs.
Need a networking and optics pass: Ethernet switching, InfiniBand exposure, 800G/1.6T optical modules, DSPs, lasers, coherent optics, retimers, and connectivity suppliers.

Need a power-equipment pass below the company level: transformers, switchgear, breakers, busway, PDUs, UPS, batteries, gas turbines, fuel cells, generators, grid interconnect equipment, and electrical contractors.
Need a liquid-cooling component pass: CDUs, cold plates, manifolds, pumps, hoses, immersion tanks, heat exchangers, chillers, and facility-level heat rejection.

Need private-market demand signal mapping for OpenAI, Anthropic, xAI, Scale AI, Crusoe, Nebius, Lambda, and other AI infrastructure/application companies where public equities are indirect suppliers or financiers.

Need market-pricing checks before ranking securities: valuation multiples, revenue exposure, backlog conversion, consensus ownership, implied AI growth, free-cash-flow pressure, debt load, and customer concentration.
Need geographic exposure mapping for U.S., Taiwan, Korea, Japan, Europe, and China because export controls, power availability, national AI policy, and supply-chain access differ materially.

Need falsification dashboard: GPU utilization, cloud AI gross margins, hyperscaler capex revisions, order cancellations, HBM pricing, CoWoS lead times, data-center power delays, grid interconnection queues, and AI software ROI evidence.

memory_update.text: AI should be tracked as a multi-layer infrastructure and automation theme, not a single-ticker story: demand propagates from hyperscaler and enterprise workloads into accelerators, HBM, foundry, packaging, networking, power, cooling, grid, construction, and software monetization.

Highest-priority Layer 1 chokepoint nodes are AI accelerators, HBM, leading-edge foundry, CoWoS-like advanced packaging, EUV lithography, AI cluster networking, data-center power equipment, liquid cooling, onsite generation, and grid interconnection.

Power and thermal infrastructure deserve a separate Layer 2 deep dive because AI deployment may be increasingly constrained by time-to-power, switchgear, transformers, backup generation, liquid cooling, and construction labor rather than only GPU availability.

The current merged universe is strongest in U.S.-listed hyperscalers and data-center infrastructure suppliers but is incomplete for Taiwan, Korea, Japan, Europe, and China semiconductor supply-chain nodes.
Before any security ranking, the next layers must validate revenue exposure, backlog quality, customer concentration, valuation pressure, capex sensitivity, utilization, and falsification indicators.

summary: Layer 1C merged the visible Layer 1A theme map and Layer 1B node-level candidates into a deduplicated initial AI universe. The universe is intentionally broad: demand owners, AI cloud platforms, accelerators, foundry/packaging, HBM/memory, lithography/equipment, networking, electrical power, cooling, onsite generation, construction/logistics, EMS, and enterprise AI software. Priority scores reflect Serenity relevance at the funnel stage, not investment merit: higher scores go to nodes closer to system expansion, hard-to-expand chokepoints, direct AI capex translation, or strong current evidence. Later layers must validate revenue exposure, pricing, valuation, customer concentration, backlog conversion, capacity, and falsification metrics.
universe_method: multi-step: theme decomposition -> node expansion -> dedupe/rank
